question: High Courts have the power to issue writs under which Article of the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __Article 226__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The High Court's power to issue writs is mentioned under Article 226.
 
• A High Court is authorized to issue directives, orders, or writs under Article 226 for the enforcement of a Fundamental Right as well as for any other reason, including writs of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari.
 
• While exercising its judicial review authority, the High Court does not serve as an appellant body.
 
• It is concerned with the unlawfulness, irrationality, and improper procedural conduct of a state or statutory authority's order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other **Important Articles**

 
 

 Article 222
 Article 222- It Deals with the Transfer of a judge from one court to another
 
 

 Article 224
 
 
• Article 224- States about the Appointment of additional and acting judges in the high court.

 
 
 

 Article 224A
